body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The fair has packed up for another year, and the closing night kept officers busy — a gunfire report that turned out to be a big fight, three missing-child calls, and a handful of other incidents across the county. Today brings more heat: a high near 103 under clear skies, no weather alerts, and no active fires reported in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The Kern County Fair closed out its run Saturday night, and the midway kept officers moving into the early hours. At 9:52 p.m., officers were sent to the carnival's amusement area on a report of shots fired, with a caller telling dispatchers people were running. The response grew quickly, but within minutes units advised there had been no gunfire at all — it was a large disturbance. Several people were seen running from the carnival area, though officers could not locate anyone involved. About 25 minutes later, officers were called to a fight in the carnival's north corner. In that same window, three missing-child calls came in: a 13-year-old girl last seen near the Bud Pavilion stage, a 2-year-old girl at the carousel, and an 11-year-old boy near the Ferris wheel.

Elsewhere, a just-occurred assault on Edwards Avenue in the metro area left a victim unconscious but breathing, and a teen girl in a red jacket and blue jeans was seen running from the scene; the victim was later conscious and talking with officers. Just after midnight, a hit-and-run on South 8th Street in south Bakersfield left officers looking for a silver Honda last seen heading west on Highway 58 from Allen Road. At 12:55 a.m., crews found a single vehicle fully engulfed in flames off the southbound side of Highway 99 north of Kimberlina Road — the occupant was already out and conscious. And at 4:45 a.m., crews responded to a rollover at Edison Highway and Tower Line; on arrival they found no ejection, with two people out of the vehicle and breathing. The rest of the log was medical aids, alarms, and traffic checks.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103 degrees today, with a low around 71 tonight. It's currently 75 degrees at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality readings were not available this morning. If you're headed out, plan around the heat — the valley's October warm spells are no joke, and the afternoon will be the hottest stretch of the day.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a 14-year-old girl was injured in a collision between her electric scooter and a vehicle in Arvin on Thursday evening, and the crash lands alongside new national data showing e-scooter injuries among children are surging.** Arvin police say the girl was riding near the CVS on Bear Mountain Boulevard around 6:40 p.m. when the crash happened; she was taken to the hospital with minor, non-life-threatening injuries. An analysis of federal injury data by E-Ride Hero estimates nearly 29,000 children aged 14 and younger were hurt in e-scooter incidents in 2025 — a 64 percent increase from 2024 and an increase of nearly 700 percent since 2020. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Joshua Deutinger told the station that as e-scooters grow in popularity, officers are seeing more crashes involving them, and he reminded parents that under California law riders need a valid driver's license to operate an e-scooter on the street, and that kids shouldn't be riding them on roadways posted above 25 miles per hour.

**According to KGET 17, a man faces life in prison after being convicted of killing his wife, with a courtroom account describing a household that neighbors and family say was marked by daily presence and, ultimately, violence.** The station's coverage centers on the trial's closing chapter and the sentence now hanging over the defendant. For Kern County readers, the case is a reminder of how domestic violence cases move through our courts and what life terms actually mean in practice.

**KGET 17 also reports that two Garces Memorial football stars have been ruled ineligible for Friday's game, leaving the status of the team's wins up in the air.** The eligibility question touches the season's record and could ripple through league standings depending on how the section rules. We'll be watching for the next step from the school and the governing body.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a Highland High student was arrested after ammunition was found in a classroom, with additional rounds later seized.** The discovery prompted a police response at the school, and the student now faces the legal consequences. It's the kind of morning-after story that has parents talking, and it's a reminder that campus safety protocols get tested in real time.

**23ABC has identified the victims of the deadly medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island that killed three people.** REACH Air Medical Services says pilot Steven "Steve" Robinson and flight nurse Jessica deVries died after the helicopter went down in the water shortly after takeoff on Sept. 30. The patient being transported, Catalina Hernandez, was also killed; her son, who was aboard, survived. Another flight nurse, Brad Sparks, continues his recovery. The crash happened well outside Kern County, but the crew's work is part of the same medical-transport network that serves communities across our region, and the loss has been felt across California's air-medical community.

**KGET 17 notes that viewers can watch the David Valadao and Randy Villegas debate — a matchup in one of the state's most closely watched congressional races.** For Kern County voters, the debate is a chance to hear the candidates directly on the issues that shape the valley, from water to agriculture to immigration. Details on how to watch are available through the station.

## Something good

A Bakersfield nonprofit is connecting community members with people held in immigration detention through pen pal letters. Wilma Goodloe spent Saturday morning at First Congregational Church joining a letter-writing session hosted by Kern Welcoming and Extending Solidarity to Immigrants, known as KWESI. Her pen pal is a 33-year-old man from Honduras she's been writing to for nearly a year — he was held at Golden State Annex in McFarland before being transferred to Texas, and he recently donated artwork for a KWESI fundraiser. KWESI Coordinator Jeannie Parent said the group visits people in detention and maintains a commissary fund, which is how it gathers names. One letter writer told the group there's nothing like the feeling of hearing your name called in the dorm and learning you have mail.

## Coming up this week

The week ahead brings a full slate of public meetings and a few nights out. The Youth Commission meets Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. On Wednesday, October 7, the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. The Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8, at noon, and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets Friday, October 9, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour" on Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." lands Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour comes through Saturday, October 17. The Fox also has a Cults & Classics season pass on sale for the 2026–2027 season.

Stay cool out there today, and if you're out early, give yourself a little extra time on the roads.

top.title: Arvin teen injured in e-scooter crash as data shows child scooter injuries up nearly 700% since 2020
